subject: Archaeology
title: The Ancestral Puebloans: Cliff Dwellers Who Left
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Ancestral Puebloans: Cliff Dwellers Who Left.

hook.text: The Ancestral Puebloans built stunning cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde — then abandoned them around 1300 CE and never returned.

buildup.text: Their cliff palaces had hundreds of rooms, towers, and kivas carved into sandstone overhangs in the American Southwest.

discovery.text: Tree-ring data shows a severe drought hit the region from 1276 to 1299 — the Great Drought devastated agriculture.

twist.text: Drought was not the only factor. Evidence of warfare, burned villages, and even cannibalism suggests social collapse.

climax.text: They did not vanish — they migrated south and became today's Pueblo peoples: Hopi, Zuni, and Rio Grande communities.

punchline.text: They were not lost. They left a home that could no longer feed them.

quiz.question: What happened to the Ancestral Puebloans of Mesa Verde?
options: They were wiped out by European diseases before Columbus arrived
They migrated south and became today's Pueblo peoples: Hopi, Zuni, and others
They moved into underground cities that have never been found

details.summary: The Ancestral Puebloans built spectacular cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde and Chaco Canyon, then abandoned them around 1300 CE. Drought, resource depletion, and social conflict drove their migration south to Pueblo communities in New Mexico and Arizona where their descendants live today.
details.whyItMatters: The Ancestral Puebloan story is often told as a mystery of disappearance, but their descendants are very much alive. Understanding their migration corrects sensationalized narratives and respects indigenous continuity.
takeaways: Built cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde and Chaco Canyon
Abandoned settlements around 1300 CE due to drought and conflict
They migrated south — their descendants are modern Pueblo peoples

faq.question: Why did the Ancestral Puebloans leave their cliff dwellings?
faq.answer: A severe drought between 1276 and 1299 made farming unsustainable in the Four Corners region. Combined with resource depletion and increasing social conflict, communities migrated south to areas with more reliable water. This was migration, not mysterious disappearance.

faq.question: Why is the term Anasazi problematic?
faq.answer: Anasazi is a Navajo word sometimes translated as ancient enemies. Modern Pueblo peoples, who are the direct descendants of these builders, prefer the term Ancestral Puebloans. Using Anasazi imposes an outsider label that modern descendants find disrespectful.
